Discover more below.

entries.title: How genome mapping can help researchers better understand disease
entries.summary: Glowing DNA double helix made of light particles, with floating A, C, T, and G letters on a dark background.
entries.content:
Your genome is your body’s instruction manual: the blueprint that informs how your body functions. It contains 3 billion base pairs of DNA. Because this DNA is responsible in part for switching genes on and off, it could be the difference between developing a disease and avoiding one. Determining which DNA changes cause diseases (and other outcomes) is like finding a needle in a haystack.

Illustrative. Your genome, one point at a time.

Decoding the DNA sequence is the goal behind AlphaGenome, a model from Google DeepMind. AlphaGenome can take a partial DNA sequence of 1 million base pairs in length, and make thousands of predictions. By comparing these predictions for DNA changes, scientists can find that needle faster.

We talked to Google DeepMind research scientist Žiga Avsec to learn more.

What do you do at Google?

ŽA: I’m a research scientist overseeing our genomics initiative. Basically, I lead a team that builds models to help us better understand the genome.

How is your team making it easier for scientists to predict and understand diseases?

It really all comes down to how the genome works. It contains 3 billion DNA base pairs. And each pair contains two bases, which we call “letters.” These letters — A (adenine), T (thymine), C (cytosine), G (guanine) — act like a biological alphabet, spelling out the genetic instruction manual that makes someone who they are.

Since you can replace any of those letters with three other letters, there are 9 billion possible single-letter changes. Many genetic diseases are caused by just one of these letters changing. But scientists don’t have time to run billions of studies to figure out which changes make a difference.

So we used AlphaGenome to predict the outcomes of all 9 billion single-letter changes, and we created a massive dataset — AlphaGenome Atlas — so scientists can decide what to research faster.

Illustrative. The letters are invented for this example.

What’s holding scientists back from better understanding the genome?

While science can read all 3 billion base pairs of human DNA, we still haven’t fully deciphered the semantics of the genetic code — particularly the non-coding "dark matter" that regulates gene expression and disease risk. Experimental research, or as it’s also called, wet-lab research is the best way to help us reach breakthroughs in our understanding, but it’s expensive and time-consuming. A single breakthrough could take years.

Let’s say you sequence DNA from a patient with a rare disease. You might end up with 4 million variants — 4 million ways their DNA differs from the standard reference human genome. But the question is: Which variant is causing their condition? Maybe you narrow the list to only include rare variants. But even then, you could be left with hundreds or thousands of options.

When scientists use AlphaGenome Atlas, they get a single, easy-to-read score — the AVI (AlphaGenome Variant Impact) score — which instantly indicates the potential impact of a variant across the full genome. This helps them prioritize and more easily find the most disruptive changes to follow up on.

Illustrative. Each dot stands for many variants. Scores are invented.

Can you give me some examples of how AlphaGenome impacts everyday people?

Tools like AlphaGenome move us from merely reading DNA to helping us better understand the molecular mechanisms behind a disease, giving researchers new leads to test and taking an important step towards someday digitally simulating a complete human cell.

There are several ways that will have an impact. It can accelerate research that could help society improve our ability to diagnose and personalize treatment for patients suffering from rare or previously uncharacterized genetic disorders. It could also speed up drug discovery pipelines by helping pharmaceutical researchers identify and validate high-probability therapeutic targets faster. Beyond healthcare, AlphaGenome’s model architecture could help researchers tackle broader societal challenges, including breeding climate-resilient crops.

Illustrative. Possible ways AlphaGenome can help.

What kinds of breakthroughs has AlphaGenome enabled?

AlphaGenome is still pretty new. We launched it in June 2025, and we just introduced AlphaGenome Atlas in September this year. But researchers are already using it to advance science.

Gareth Hawkes, a Medical Research Council fellow at the University of Exeter, used AlphaGenome Atlas to narrow down a list of 1 billion genetic variants. By focusing on the most impactful 1%, he identified 19 variant groups linked to body mass index to prioritize in his research.

And Laura Covill, a Broad Institute research fellow, used the AVI score to prioritize genetic variants in their research of unsolved rare diseases. AlphaGenome Atlas identified a critical variant in a gene linked to neurodevelopmental disorders, providing crucial supporting evidence that drove their subsequent research, including solving the case.

What are you hoping to do next?

We just launched our latest model, AlphaGenome 2, which tackles one of the key limitations of AlphaGenome: cell type specificity. While AlphaGenome is state-of-the-art, it was trained mostly on data from whole tissues or cell lines. We know that individual cell types in those tissues have a very specific role and can malfunction in disease. AlphaGenome 2 moves beyond tissue-level averages to predict how genetic variants disrupt these individual cell types, helping researchers pinpoint the cellular drivers of disease.

We’re also actively researching better ways to measure how confident our model is in its predictions so researchers know how much to trust each result. From early analyses, we see that variants with strongly predicted effects are quite good and achieve high levels of accuracy. As always, anyone using AlphaGenome should interpret its predictions with other sources of information.

What's the ultimate goal of your work in biology?

In the short term, we’d like to use AI to better understand the grammar of the genome and accurately predict the effects of mutations. In the long term, we’d like to build on this foundation towards a fully functioning digital simulation of a human cell.

This will allow researchers to computationally model disease mechanisms, understand rare genetic conditions, and test candidate therapies.

entries.title: See what 5 builders are making with Gemini 4 Carbon
entries.summary: Collage of different projects made with Gemini 4 Carbon
entries.content:
Gemini 4 Carbon was built for tasks that push the limits of a model’s intelligence, and builders are putting it to the test.

Since we rolled out Carbon more broadly last week, we've seen the community lean into the model’s ability to explore thoroughly, reason deeply, and run extended verification loops. Find five impressive projects that demonstrate Carbon's capabilities below.

Render a wind-swept meadow.

Glitter Gal (@GlitterPixely on X) coded a meadow of 52,000 wildflowers and grass blades from scratch in CUDA and C++ with Carbon, synthesizing the wind to match every gust.

Create a simulation with a million moving parts.

Chubby (@kimmonismuson X) wanted to see over a million glowing particles swirl and shift like live tidal currents, using Carbon to simulate 1,048,576 particles in real time with WebGPU.

Make a glass game that shatters.

Andrew V (@AI_Andrew on X) wondered what a block-stacking game would feel like if every piece were made of fragile stained glass; Carbon simulated how the tower catches the light, rings when tapped, and shatters into shards when it falls.

Turn disorganized data into interactive tools.

Giyu_codes (@giyu_codes on X) went looking for underserved industries buried in messy public records, pairing with Carbon to turn scattered public datasets into 14 interactive tools with live 3D visuals. Explore all 14 builds in their thread.

Build a mesmerizing laboratory.

Starting from a single reference image, The Bugged Dev (@thebuggeddev on X) brought a 19th-century Parisian optics lab to life with Carbon, complete with 92 brass and glass instruments you can actually test and tune.

Developers can build with Carbon with the Gemini API paid tier in Google AI Studio and Android Studio. Google AI Ultra subscribers can try it in Google Antigravity, AI Studio, the Gemini app, and AI Mode in Search. And Gemini for business users can access it via the API or model drop down, Google Antigravity, or CodeMender.

entries.title: Read the EmbeddingGemma 2 technical report.
entries.summary: The Google EmbeddingGemma 2 technical report details our new multimodal model, covering its unified vector space and compact design. Read the report.
entries.content:
We released EmbeddingGemma 2, which expands our text-only open embedding model with native multimodal understanding. It maps text, images, audio, and video, or any combination of them, into a single embedding space, all while compressing the model backbone into a more compact profile.

You can now get in-depth information about our training strategy, evaluation methodology, and experimental results in the official technical report. The model’s recipe features innovations that build on top of the latest technology from Gemma 4 and Gemini Embedding 2, enabling EmbeddingGemma 2 to learn an expressive and unified vector space.

Watch our five-minute explainer to see how EmbeddingGemma 2 works and how it was developed.

entries.title: Put Gemini to work for you
entries.summary: A user interface displaying the prompt "What can I get done for you?" above an input box containing placeholder text "Describe a task".
entries.content:
The best assistant knows you and helps you get things done. Today, you can now hand off even more tasks to Gemini and move on with your day. We’ve built it for anyone who has tasks piling up during all the classes, meetings, and school drop-offs that fill the day. Our goal is for Gemini to save you time and money.

Starting now, this update is rolling out free of charge for hundreds of millions of people across the U.S., Japan, Korea, Canada, Australia, and India, using our new Gemini 4 Hydrogen model. We’re also rolling out a set of advanced features, starting in the U.S.

How it’s changing my daily routine

If your emails, calendar, passwords, photos, files, and payment cards are already in the Google ecosystem, Gemini is your best choice as a personal assistant because this sensitive data already lives at Google securely, and you don’t have to send it elsewhere.

Here’s how I’m using it.

Recently, our minivan’s check-engine light came on. Ugh. I pulled out Gemini and told it, "Our minivan is overdue for a service appointment. Please call the two nearest dealerships and figure out how to get an appointment early Friday morning over the next month or so."

Because Gemini already knows we drive a 2019 Honda Odyssey and where we live through Personal Intelligence, it found the nearest shops on Google Maps and called both at once 1 . Thankfully, I didn’t have to suffer through any hold music. Gemini did the job, found a time in my Google Calendar when I was free, and added the Friday early morning appointment in less than five minutes. Done. (On the dealership's end, Gemini disclosed right away that it's an AI. Businesses can opt out whenever they want, and Gemini won’t give out my payment or private account info unless I say so.)

In the background, Gemini called both dealerships at once, sat through the hold music for me, booked an appointment at the shop that accepts appointments vs. walk-ins only, and put Friday's appointment on my calendar without me having to check it.

Last month it saved us real money after we got hit with a surprise $389 electric bill. I gave Gemini permission to access our utility portal with the new Google Password Manager integration and asked for it to analyze our past billing statements in my email. Gemini worked for a few minutes, and then nailed it. The primary culprit was our heat pump, which it turns out was kicking on around 4 p.m., right in the middle of peak pricing. My wife and I never would have caught that digging through the PDFs and emails ourselves.

I use it for smaller stuff, too. For our upcoming holiday trip back to Oklahoma, I recently asked Gemini to give me the best options for a USB-C charger. Gemini quickly compared chargers thanks to Google’s Shopping Graph, asked me follow-up questions about the wattage and color, and then helped me check out using the new Google Pay integration. The best part: it also found a discount code so I saved an extra $10. Done.

Gemini now uses the Agent Payments Protocol (AP2) to make purchases like this. We’re working with American Express (coming soon), Mastercard, and Visa to keep your purchases secure with digital tokens on supported cards. And when you shop with Gemini, you still earn your card's points, cashback, or purchase protections during checkout. You can also set a hard spending cap upfront, and Gemini is designed to stay within your budget. All of your receipts and tracking info land straight in Google Wallet, which is expanding to iOS starting today. Up next, we’ll integrate the Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) into Gemini so everyone can expect an even faster and more reliable shopping experience from discovery to checkout.

Gemini lets you set the spending limit and still earn every airline mile, cashback point, and perk on your card.

Gemini helps with weeknight dinners, too. I recently stared down a nearly empty fridge rushing out the door in the morning, and I texted Gemini with the new RCS integration 2 : “Add lasagna, strawberries, cucumbers, and vanilla ice cream to our Instacart order.” On the walk out, I saw an empty Cheerios box in the pantry, so I snapped a photo and sent a quick follow-up: “Add this too.” Gemini added it, and then handed me off to Instacart to complete the order. Groceries were on the doorstep when we got home. Done. Today, Gemini connects with more than 60 popular apps and, as a developer, you can apply to join our Connected Apps Platform.

My wife and I also use Gemini to sort out medical bills, keep track of insurance renewals, and stay on top of our kids' schedules. Earlier this week, I forwarded a batch of school emails from Gmail to gemini@google.com. In less than a minute, every date was on my calendar with my wife invited. Better yet, it noticed a conflict during basketball practice and asked if I wanted to text one of the other parents to trade carpool duty.

How we protect your data

As Gemini becomes more capable, we continually advance our security defenses. When you assign Gemini a task, it uses Google Cloud’s Agent Compute Engine to work in a hardware-isolated virtual machine that’s dedicated to your account and never shared with other users. Each virtual machine is sandboxed, so Gemini works in a separate, isolated environment that’s regularly tested by our security red teams. This sandbox is just one of multiple layers of defense, including prompt-injection filters that scan search results, webpages, and more alongside Google Safe Browsing to limit which links Gemini can open.

As Gemini works on a task, you can jump in to give it more instructions at any point, and it’s also designed to pause and check with you before critical steps. For example, Gemini is designed to ask for your confirmation or pre-approval before clicking "Buy," and will ask clarifying questions if an instruction is ambiguous. For routine stuff you already trust, like adding those Cheerios to your grocery cart, you can set that to “Always allow” so it doesn’t pester you.

And finally, we give you access to settings and tools that help you safeguard your data and protect your privacy. You can adjust task settings, disconnect Google and third-party apps, or delete chat history anytime. For a closer look at how we’ve implemented a multi-layer defense-in-depth security strategy, read our technical paper.

And please participate in our bug bounty program through Google’s AI Vulnerability Reward Program (AI VRP) to advance the security of agentic systems.

How you can help us improve

While we’ve tested tasks extensively to minimize mistakes, we haven't eliminated all of them. You may encounter situations where a task fails to complete or misses the mark. When you see this, please provide feedback by giving the response a “thumbs down.”

For example, the way personal assistants navigate the web is still evolving as sites are still adapting to these new use cases. On some sites, Gemini can make it most of the way through and then hand the screen back to you to click the final button. We’re partnering directly with major websites and security providers to help the web evolve so it works well for site owners and personal assistants. For decades, bots were blocked by default because most were malicious. Personal assistants require a more nuanced approach, and we believe open, verifiable standards will benefit everyone.

How to try it

Ready to hand off your next task? Open Gemini, flip the home-screen toggle from Chat to Task, and tell Gemini what you need done. Starting in the U.S., you can also forward emails to gemini@google.com or text Gemini by following these instructions:

  • Open Gemini on Android or iOS and tap Settings
  • Tap Channels
  • Tap Set up under Text with Gemini
  • Verify your phone number

We can’t wait to see what Gemini crosses off your list first.

entries.title: 10 states team up with Google on free AI training
entries.summary: Two people work on a computer
entries.content:
Today, seven in 10 managers believe an AI-trained workforce is critical to their organization’s success, yet they aren’t offering the practical training that would help. We want to make it easy for everyone to learn how to use technology effectively and responsibly when it’s convenient for them, wherever they live and work.

That’s what led Grow with Google to partner with states across the country to bring no-cost training directly to residents. We started in Oklahoma. Then, we partnered with Massachusetts, where nearly 40,000 residents signed up through the MassTech AI Hub within six months of launch.

North Carolina is now our tenth state partner to offer our digital and AI training at no cost to residents through NC LIVE. It joins Arkansas, Connecticut, Delaware, Georgia, Massachusetts, Missouri, Oklahoma, South Dakota and Virginia.

Meeting learners in the places they trust

While each partnership shapes the rollout to fit their communities, they share the common goal of making digital and AI training accessible to everyone.

  • Partnering with public libraries: In Georgia, Oklahoma and North Carolina, statewide library systems are the front door. Residents can check out digital resources, and take foundational courses at no cost. In North Carolina, this builds on Google's broader AI work across the state. For example, Google is the founding partner for the first-of-its-kind Institute for Artificial Intelligence and Emerging Research at North Carolina Central University, an institute dedicated to researching ethical AI and expanding student pathways.
  • Teaching students career skills: In Missouri, state education and workforce agencies partnered to offer digital training across K-12 systems, colleges, universities, and local Missouri job centers. In Connecticut, Charter Oak State College launched an Online AI Academy to bring practical AI skills to residents across the state. This expanded reach builds on our work with over 500 education institutions across all 50 states who are part of the Google AI for Education Accelerator, a no-cost program to help students, faculty and staff with AI and other job-ready skills.
  • Driving local economic growth: States like Virginia, Delaware, and Arkansas are integrating AI coursework directly into state workforce programs, economic development councils, and job centers, making sure state workers, career seekers, and local businesses can put AI to work right away.

Building confidence through practical skills

We hear from people across career fields that they want to know more about AI, but they tell us it can be intimidating to get started.

We created the Google AI Professional Certificate to help them succeed. Through this training course they learn how to use AI to create marketing materials, gain insights from their data, prepare presentations, build their own apps and much more. And they practice hands-on with real examples.

Learn more at grow.google/gov.

entries.title: Temporary threads are now available in AI Mode in Search.
entries.summary: Google AI Mode now offers temporary threads for private searches. Keep your history clean and avoid personalization. Try this new feature today.
entries.content:
We’re introducing temporary threads in AI Mode, where you can explore and ask questions — whether that’s brainstorming a surprise gift or looking something up you don’t want resurfaced later like in your history or recommendations.

There’s no need to adjust your settings — you can quickly jump into a temporary thread for any query you don't want saved, and switch right back when you're done. To get started, simply click the temporary threads icon in the upper right corner of AI Mode and start asking your questions. Because your session is completely detached from your account, your responses won’t be informed by past preferences, affect future personalization, or be saved to your history. Once you close the thread, it’s gone, letting you go back to searching as usual.

This feature is rolling out globally on desktop and mobile browsers across all languages supported in AI Mode.

entries.title: From easier entry to smarter savings, here’s what’s new in Google Home.
entries.summary: Google Home updates bring keyless entry, smarter audio alerts, and faster Gemini performance. See what’s new in the November 2026 update.
entries.content:
From unlocking your front door to trimming utility bills, here’s what’s new across Google Home:

  • Keyless entry: Android users can now unlock compatible front doors with a quick tap or hands-free approach using digital home keys in Google Wallet.
  • Smarter alerts: For added peace of mind, Google Home Premium Advanced now detects audio — like barking dogs or breaking glass — in motion-triggered camera and doorbell event descriptions.
  • Nest thermostat upgrades: Starting in December, Nest thermostat owners in the U.S. and Canada can check the app to see estimated cumulative savings. And they can also balance hot and cold spots with compatible third-party room sensors with their 4th-gen Nest Learning Thermostat.
  • Faster Gemini for Home: Gemini for Home now handles everyday requests up to 20% faster and is expanding to six new countries, including India and Brazil.

To learn more about the latest updates to Google Home, visit the Nest Community.

entries.title: Anyone can create a personal avatar of themselves in Google Vids, at no cost.
entries.summary: Create custom avatars in Google Vids for free. Design your digital likeness using a selfie and voice recording to narrate videos. Try it out today.
entries.content:
Personal avatars in Google Vids lets you create a custom digital avatar to star in your videos. Starting today, we’re bringing personal avatars to everyone with a personal Google account, at no cost.

Take it for a spin:

  • Make it your own. Design a custom avatar with the look and voice that fits your vision.
  • Skip the filming setup. Scan a QR code to create your personal avatar likeness, and see it automatically added to your video prompt. From there, just type what you want to say and create.
  • Keep it consistent. Your avatar is saved to your Vids project, so you can reuse it across every scene.

Personal avatars are linked to your Google Account and are restricted to the account holder’s likeness. Head to vids.new on desktop to try it out.
